title: How Latent Transition Geometry Matters for Planning in World Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.30064v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: World models support planning by predicting how the environment evolves under candidate actions. However, one-step predictive accuracy alone does not characterize multi-step planning utility, which depends on distinguishing candidate futures. This raises a natural question: How does latent transition geometry shape planning? We investigate this through an action-conditioned transition-field view, using curvature regularization as a controlled intervention. Across four continuous-control tasks, appropriately tuned regularization improves planning, while excessive regularization can be detrimental. By decomposing the transition field into affine and non-affine components, we find that regularization reduces action sensitivity mainly through the non-affine component. To assess its role in planning, we directly manipulate the non-affine action response in frozen models and show that it affects candidate selection and closed-loop success. Fur

translated_title: 潜空间转移几何如何影响世界模型中的规划
translated_abstract: 世界模型通过预测环境在候选动作下的演化来支持规划。然而，仅凭单步预测精度并不能刻画多步规划的效用，后者取决于能否区分不同的候选未来。这引出了一个自然的问题：潜在转移几何如何塑造规划？我们通过动作条件化的转移场视角来研究这一问题，并将曲率正则化作为一种受控干预手段。在四个连续控制任务上，适当调节的正则化能够改善规划性能，而过度正则化则可能有害。通过将转移场分解为仿射与非仿射分量，我们发现正则化主要是通过非仿射分量来降低动作敏感性。为评估其在规划中的作用，我们在冻结模型中直接操纵非仿射动作响应，结果表明它会影响候选选择与闭环任务的成功率。
tldr: 该论文从动作条件化的潜在转移几何视角出发，发现通过曲率正则化塑造转移场的非仿射动作响应能够显著改善世界模型的多步规划性能。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that shaping the latent transition geometry of world models through curvature regularization—mainly via the non-affine component of the action-conditioned transition field—improves multi-step planning performance.
